prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
The API now needs a Bearer API key and checks its role (viewer, cook or manager). A missing or unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized` and a known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`. Every non-GET request made with a known key writes an audit entry, and managers can read them newest first at `GET /audit`. `npm test` (30 tests passing) and `npm run lint` both pass. The test helper now sends the manager key by default, and the new `tests/access.test.js` covers the 401, 403, cook-permission and audit cases.

Things to know:
- `data/db.json`, the default file for `npm start`, still has no keys, so a locally started server will answer 401 to everything until you add keys to it or copy them from `data/seed.json`.
- I did not bump the schema version. `apiKeys` and `audit` are optional collections, the same way `outbox`, `stocktakes` and `temperatures` were added.
- Audit entries include failed and 403 requests, so they record the status. Requests with no key or an unknown key are not audited. Writing an audit entry saves the store a second time after the route's own save.
- For stock-takes, cooks can enter counts but cannot start or finish a stock-take; those need a manager.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
